title: Clamp a hanging file folder around a packet and hang it on frame rails
instruction: Hang the file folder on both top rails of the file frame with the document packet still inside it.
context: Filing and maintaining paper records in hanging file drawers and desktop frames is core work for general office clerks (O*NET 43-9061.00, 'File and maintain records'; BLS May 2024: 2,510,550 US jobs) and file clerks (43-4071.00). Closest look-alikes: TK-BFJD6N (hang a rigid blind headrail in two gated wall brackets) and TK-7FTC8C (snap a rigid module onto one DIN rail). Here the robot must pinch both top hanger rods of an un-sprung V-hinged folder shut around a loose 200 g paper packet so the pages cannot slip out during the 90 deg pitch, then lower all four rod-end hook saddles simultaneously onto two parallel steel frame rails ahead of existing filed folders.
setup: Two 6-DOF arms with parallel-jaw grippers sit at (0.00, +0.305) m and (0.00, -0.305) m along the near edge of a station desk (top z = 0.7475 m). Six 1:1 objects sit on the desk: (1) a fixed natural oak wood pickup block (200 x 130 x 32 mm, < USD 5) clamped at (0.1750, 0.0000) m with dark corner alignment marks on top so the folder's hanger rods overhang both sides by 99 mm; (2) a fixed Officemate 91990 letter-size steel hanging file frame (~USD 14) set to its 14 in (355.6 mm) depth from x = 0.4250 m to 0.7806 m (317.6 mm center-to-center rail span at y = +-0.1588 m, 238 mm rail height to z = 0.9855 m, with a 4 mm-high front U-saddle bottom bar leaving a 311.6 x 226 mm open front throat); (3) a loose V-hinged Pendaflex 4152 letter-size green hanging file folder (~USD 18 per 25-pack; two 298.5 x 230 x 2.5 mm matte pressboard leaves with lighter kraft-sage interior joined at an un-sprung 9.2 mm bottom V-gusset crease hinge, each topped by a 328 mm white coated-steel hanger rod with underside rail-hook saddles at y = +-0.1588 m, plus a clip-on 52 x 12.5 mm blue 1/5-cut index tab at y = +0.044 m and ruled front file label, 0.16 kg total) resting flat on the oak pickup block with its bottom crease at x = 0.0720 m and overhanging top rods at x = 0.3045 m; (4) a loose trimmed paper document packet (~60 sheets, 200 g estimated) in a trimmed 1/3-cut manila folder cover (280 x 195 x 6.0 mm interior stack at x = 0.1770 m with an exposed 62 x 180 x 4.0 mm printed white top-sheet header and 12 x 88 x 2.0 mm left 1/3-cut manila tab protruding cleanly between the two hanger rods, 0.20 kg total); and (5)-(6) two loose already-filed Pendaflex 4152 green hanging folders (0.22 kg each, containing visible white pages and Smead manila tabs with staggered amber and clear 1/5-cut index tabs at y = -0.062 m and +0.092 m) pre-hung by their four hook saddles on the rear half of the frame rails at x = 0.6350 m and x = 0.7100 m.
scoring: Final state only; the untouched starting layout scores 0. 0 if any folder or packet lies more than 30 mm below the desk. Every positive score requires all six independent pad/jaw points at least 80 mm from every folder (target and both rear filed folders), packet, frame, and wood block surface, and less than 1 mm extremal-point movement across all folders and the packet over the last 21 samples at 20 Hz. 0.5: each of the target folder's four rod-end hooks straddles its own rail between both retaining lugs, with the rail top bearing under the rod and the folder crease at least 5 mm above the desk. In simulation, the complete 3.6 mm rail width and its upper 2 mm must fit inside the 7.2 mm saddle void at both faces of each 3 mm-thick hook, with rail top-to-bearing separation in [0, 0.50] mm (allowing at most 0.10 mm solver penetration), zero lateral tolerance outside the retaining lugs, and all tested rail sections within the 355.6 mm rail length. 1.0: 0.5 holds and the packet remains inside the target V-folder, its centre between the leaves, its span within the folder width plus 10 mm, and its lowest point at least 5 mm above the desk; otherwise 0. Real trial: verify 1.0 s stillness on synchronised overhead and side video, measure >= 80 mm gripper clearance with a tape measure, check >= 5 mm crease and packet clearance above the desk with a ruler, and photograph both ends of the left and right rails square-on so both lugs of all four target hooks visibly flank the rail blade (a rod or lug tip balanced outside its saddle scores 0). Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 1.0.
fidelity: Frame and folders match 1:1 Officemate 91990 frame at 14 in depth (355.6 x 317.6 x 238 mm) and Pendaflex 4152 letter folders (328 mm rods, 298.5 x 230 mm leaves). Target leaves, 200 g printed paper/manila stack, and two loose rear filed folders are rigid proxies with visual page edges/ink and estimated 3.6 mm rail in 7.2 mm saddle, damping (0.02), and friction (0.45-0.58); paper flex is omitted. Open-loop demo; nothing moved or latched by code.
reset_notes: Confirm both rails sit at their 317.6 mm spacing and 238 mm height, and re-seat the two rear filed folders on the rails at x = 0.635 m and 0.710 m. Place the same 200 g printed paper and Smead 1/3-cut manila packet inside the target folder with its printed header and manila tab protruding 42 mm past the rods, and lay both leaves flat on the 200 x 130 x 32 mm oak pickup block at the alignment marks. Inspect all hook saddles for bent lugs before each trial. No consumables or heating.
